appraisal_events.evidence: "Aimé, vous pourrez dire à M. de Stermaria qu'il n'est pas le seul noble qu'il y ait dans cette salle à manger... c'est le marquis de Cambremer," said "insidieusement" after Stermaria's absence was noted "au grand regret du bâtonnier."
appraisal_events.explanation: An unnamed local dining companion (a role-designated figure not on the reference sheet, hence recorded as an unresolved source) insidiously undercuts Stermaria's presumed uniqueness as the room's resident noble by citing marquis de Cambremer's presence, relaying the jab through Aimé since Stermaria is not there to hear it.

status_effects.explanation: Stermaria's implicit distinction as the recognized noble of the dining room is challenged behind his back, though the put-down is indirect, mediated, and he never witnesses it, limiting its force.

ambiguities: The actual speaker of the insidious remark ('le bâtonnier') is identified only by professional title, not a proper name, and does not appear on the reference sheet as a reviewed entry; per scope rules he is excluded from characters_present and the event's source is recorded as 'unknown' even though the passage clearly attributes the remark to him.
